question: to the Commission Veronika Vrecionová (ECR) Subject:

In its answer to question E-002824/20261, the Commission states that the principle of proportionality was integral to the development of the EU rules. However, the answer does not specify whether the proportionality of the requirements for the collection and disposal of blood was assessed specifically in relation to small family farms which slaughter only one or a few animals per year on their holding. In view of the very limited scale of such slaughters, could the Commission therefore respond specifically in relation to this situation, and not merely by reference to the general principles of the applicable hygiene provisions: 1.

Was the proportionality of the requirements for the handling of blood on small farms carrying out only occasional slaughter specifically assessed during the adoption or subsequent review of Regulation (EC) 1069/2009?
Do the current rules allow Member States to apply a simplified regime in such cases, while maintaining the necessary veterinary, hygiene and environmental safeguards?

If the current rules do not provide for such a possibility, will the Commission, when reviewing them in the future, consider introducing a more proportionate regime for small farms carrying out only occasional slaughter?
